title: U.S. House · Minnesota's 4th District
area: Saint Paul and its eastern and northern suburbs, including Woodbury, Maplewood and Shoreview.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Betty McCollum (D) defeated Aswar Rahman in the Democratic primary, 85.7%-14.3%. Paul Wikstrom, an engineering manager who previously ran unsuccessfully for a Minnesota House special election in 2025, won the Republican primary over Paul Xiong and Gene Rechtzigel with 72.6% of the vote.

candidates.name: Betty McCollum

summary.text: Betty McCollum is the Democratic incumbent seeking re-election in Minnesota's 4th Congressional District, which she has represented since 2001.

background.text: Born in 1954 in Minneapolis, Minnesota; graduated from South St. Paul High School and earned a B.A. from the College of St. Catherine in St. Paul.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Appropriations, on the Interior, Environment and Related Agencies and Defense subcommittees, in the 119th Congress; previously chaired and served as ranking member of the Defense subcommittee in earlier Congresses.

candidates.researchNotes: Key floor votes and FEC finance totals for this sitting member of Congress are added separately; this entry focuses on biography, committee roles and record.

candidates.name: Paul Wikstrom
candidates.ballotNote: Won the Republican primary over Paul Xiong and Gene Rechtzigel with 72.6% of the vote.

summary.text: Paul Wikstrom is the Republican nominee challenging Rep. Betty McCollum. He is an engineering manager from Shoreview who previously ran unsuccessfully for a Minnesota House special election in 2025.

background.text: Grew up in Montana and North Dakota before moving to Minnesota as a young adult; earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Minnesota, Twin Cities, and a graduate degree from the University of St. Thomas.
Worked in seismic exploration, road construction and farming before becoming an engineer; currently works as an engineering manager.
Lost the March 11, 2025 special general election for Minnesota House District 40B to David Gottfried (D), 70.2%-29.8%.
Has been married 30 years and raised three children in Shoreview, Minnesota.

priorities.text: Protecting jobs, cutting regulatory red tape on local industries, and letting working Americans keep more of their paychecks.
priorities.quote: My experiences have shaped my priorities as a candidate: protecting jobs, cutting the red tape that stifles our local industries, and making sure that hard working Americans keep more of their hard-earned paychecks.

positions.summary: Says his priority is making sure working Americans keep more of their paychecks, framing his campaign around reducing the tax and regulatory burden on workers and local industry.

candidates.researchNotes: Wikstrom's Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey response was brief and covered mainly biography; no separate campaign website with a detailed issues page was found within the research budget for this race.
